reasons: The cited text (Section 20.1) is indeed a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity with no Vendor indemnity, which is the rule's walk-away position; the 'missing' classification is correct and actionable.

The redline reaches the preferred position in full: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, injury and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; customary IP exclusions and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies; and Customer's indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is explained by the rule itself: a one-sided indemnity section must be rewritten to add the Vendor obligation and narrow ours, so the high changed-character ratio is justified rather than gratuitous.

Placing the infringement remedies at 20.5 sensibly cures the dangling cross-reference from Section 9.3, and the retained Customer indemnity is preserved (renumbered to 20.2) rather than deleted, so no protection is lost for the counterparty beyond the intended narrowing.

The comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, correctly prefixed, and states both what changed and why with reference to the playbook position; omission of the 3× super-cap fallback is reasonable given indemnity claims are already carved out of the cap as Excluded Claims.

Minor residual risk only: the redline relies on terms (Affiliates, Deliverables, Vendor Technology, Security Incident, Applicable Law) not shown in the resolved definitions, and renumbering the Customer indemnity to 20.2 should be checked against any cross-references (e.g., in Section 21.3) — worth a conforming-references pass but not a defect in the position taken.
